title: lathe add refuses a write the command layer refuses, printing the reason, and changes nothing
when: Runs writes the command layer refuses: an aggregate under a domain that does not exist, one whose ID is outside its domain, a view with no title, and refused sets, moves, links and table rules. Calls the add tool with a new requirement, then with a use case that does not exist, an entity field with no type, and two tables in one call.
then: Expects every reason printed, an exit code of 1 and the data files unchanged. Expects the row on success and every reason on a refusal.

title: Text with quotes, newlines and backticks given as JSON is written exactly, from stdin or a file, in every write tool's shape
when: Adds a requirement from stdin and sets a use case's goal from a file, each with quotes, newlines, backticks, tabs and accents, then links, unlinks, sets, clears, adds and removes through --json -. Pipes an add under a domain that does not exist as JSON and gives the same add as flags, then pipes an array with an item naming two tables and an item that is not an object. Pipes JSON to `--json -` together with a field flag, a parent flag or a table name, to `lathe show`, as text that does not parse and as an empty array, and names a JSON file that does not exist. Pipes an array of two views as one add, then an array whose second view's ID is taken.
then: Expects the text read back exactly, the same line the flag form writes, and each write done. Expects the same refusal as the flag form, each item of the wrong shape named, and the data files unchanged. Expects exit 2 with the reason, and the data files unchanged. Expects two records added by one array, and nothing written when one item of another array is refused.

title: A cold lathe show takes under 800 ms
when: `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf`. Runs `lathe show LA-PLT-UC01` on a copy of Lathe's repo in a fresh process once to fill the schema cache, then five times more.
then: Expects the median, from the process's start to its exit, under 800 ms. On a busy machine (a one-minute load average above 12) it judges nothing and exits 3.

title: A cached schema gives what one built afresh gives, and is used without being built again
when: Loads the fixture with no cache, then twice with an empty cache folder. Changes a migration's text, and, separately, stamps each cache file with another key and an altered schema. Overwrites Lathe's cache file with garbage, then with its first third, then the product's file with garbage, loading after each. Starts two processes at once on the fixture with an empty cache folder.
then: Expects the same schema, placements, parents and tables each time (no trace of the cache's stamp), one file for Lathe's schema and one for the fixture's kinds, and the second load to leave both files as they were. Expects a changed migration to change the key, and the next load to give what a fresh build gives, replace both files and remove an older base schema's file; the load after uses the files as they are. Expects each load to give what a fresh build gives, and the file to be whole again after it. Expects both to print what a fresh build gives, the folder to hold the two cache files and nothing half-written, and a load after to use them as they are.

title: A held record shows the rows that hold it marked, an untraced one says so over the rows around it, and an entity shows its aggregate's rows
when: Opens on the Trace stage a command a chain holds, a test, a command nothing traces to and an entity.
then: Expects the held command `P-D-CMD01` marked in three rows (`P-D-DS01`, `P-D-SP01`, `P-D-UC01-R01`) and "3 obligations hold this record" in the header strip; the test marked in its obligation's row; for the untraced `P-D-CMD02` "Nothing traces to this record: it serves no requirement or rule." above its aggregate's matrix (`P-D-INV01`, `P-D-INV02`), the command marked in the Untraced section; and for the entity its aggregate's matrix with no untraced warning, "This record sits outside every chain" and "Outside the chains · matrix of Loan" in the header strip.

title: Panels collapse for space wiki card first, then the nav, never the chat or a tool, and titles never break mid-word
when: Works out the panels collapsed for space at 1920, 1456, 1440, 1280 and 1024 px with every panel and the chat open, at 1440, 1280 and 1024 px without the chat, with a panel closed and with one held open, and reads every stylesheet.
then: Expects, with the chat and without it, nothing collapsed in a wide window, then the wiki card, then the card and the nav to its rail as the window narrows, the stage keeping 300 px at each width; a closed panel never counted; the chat and a tool over the stage never collapsed; a held wiki card making the nav give way; the card's CSS limits read from the shell's minimums; and no `word-break: break-all` and no title with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`.

title: On a record page a narrow window collapses the wiki card, then the nav, each toggle saying so, and they come back as it widens
when: Opens a use case on the Graph stage in a 1000 px window, opens the wiki card from its toggle, then sets the window to 1920, 1000, 600 and back to 1920 px.
then: Expects the wiki card collapsed for space with its toggle saying so, the nav giving way once the card is opened anyway, every panel back at 1920 px with no toggle marked, the card and then the nav collapsing as the window narrows with the nav's remembered choice untouched, and every panel back at 1920 px.

title: The Trace tree is laid out once: focusing two records and toggling Gaps only moves no box
when: Lays out a product's Trace tree, then works out the focus of a requirement and of a command and the fades with and without Gaps only.
then: Expects every box at the same place and size before and after, the same tree for the same product and data, and a new tree, laid out once, for new data.

title: The ERD map is laid out once: focusing two records moves no box, and the layout is read again for the same data
when: Asks for a product's ERD map and its layout twice on the same data and once on new data, then opens a domain on the ERD stage and focuses an aggregate by a click and an entity by Enter.
then: Expects the same map and layout for the same data, a new map laid out once for new data, and every box's place and size on the page the same before and after each focus.

title: Every tool is an overlay in the address of the focus it is over, opened in order, closed topmost first, carried to a new focus, and counted in the open space
when: Applies address patches, reads the overlays of several queries, carries them to new addresses, parses the old full-screen addresses, works out the open space and crowding with a tool open, and reads the dialog and panel sources.
then: Expects each patch to replace its parameters at the end and drop empty ones, the topmost overlay to be the last opened, Escape's link to close it, a tool (never a format page) carried to a new focus, the old addresses to be no pages, a tool to shrink the open space and the wiki card to give way to it, and the dialogs and panels to share one focus hook.

title: Checks, Appearance, the theme editor, a format page and the products picker each open over the stage, which keeps its focus; Escape closes the topmost and focus returns
when: On a use case, opens Checks from the nav, a check's page from it, Appearance, the theme editor and quick open over Checks, pressing Escape after each; then opens the products picker.
then: Expects each tool floating at the left with the stage and its focus still there, the check's page in the wiki card, Escape closing the card's page, then the panel, focus back on the nav's Checks link, quick open closing alone before the panel, and the picker over the dimmed, inert stage of the last product, Escape going back to it.

title: The Graph, ERD and Trace stages show the same controls in the same order and places, folding them in one fixed order
when: On a use case, opens the Graph stage, then the ERD, then the Trace, and reads each stage's toolbar and camera; reads the toolbar's forms; then opens the Graph with a toolbar too narrow for the Changes controls and depth.
then: Expects one toolbar at the top of the open space on each, its step buttons Left, Right, Up, Down, Out and In then Frame first, the stage's own controls after them (none on the ERD, Gaps only on the Trace) and no Key; each step showing its arrow and letter; the camera's Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit the whole map in the corner, and no React Flow controls. Expects the forms, widest first, to hide the names and the baseline picker, then fold the Changes controls into More, then depth, then drop the step letters, and to fold the steps only in the last (the phone's), never Frame or the primary controls; and on the narrow Graph the steps with their letters, Frame, the layouts and the filters in the row, More at its end holding the Changes controls with the baseline picker, then depth.

title: On Lathe's own spec every node each stage draws is reached by keyboard from the product
when: Loads Lathe's spec with its chains, and from the product searches breadth first over every move of the walk (the four arrows, Out and In): on the Graph in each layout, on the ERD over its laid-out map, on the Trace over its tree.
then: Expects every box of the Graph's map in each layout, every region, aggregate area and entity of the ERD, and every box of the Trace's tree reached, naming any that is not.

title: A field's input follows its column's type
when: Renders the shared ColumnField for an enum, a whole number, a list of texts, a required and an optional true or false, and a line and a long text, and turns texts into values.
then: Expects a select, a number, a text area, a checkbox, a select, an input and a text area, each labeled and described by its column, and each text the value its column takes, a text not of its type left for the command to refuse.

title: A shared field input knows no kind
when: Reads the shared field inputs' file.
then: Expects it to import nothing of the specs, the aggregates' slices, the shell, the graph or the views, and to name no kind.

title: The record actions take only a known action and a record ID, and find the data file themselves
when: Accepts each action with a record ID. Run `npm --prefix desktop start` and open a record page. Choose Reveal in Finder: Finder shows the record's data file selected. Choose Open in editor: the file opens in the editor at the record's line. Choose Copy ID and paste it: the record's ID. Change the record's title in the editor and save: the page shows the new title within a second or two.
then: Refuses paths, unknown actions, lower-case and malformed IDs and extra keys; finds the data file whose row starts with the record's ID, never one that only names it, and again after it changes; and builds the native menu. It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: Open in editor uses VS Code by default, another known editor, the default app or a command of one's own
when: Reads settings with VS Code as the fallback, opens known editors by bundle ID on macOS and by command elsewhere, passes the file to a custom command as an argument and never in its text, and names the editor for the menu. Builds the menus and clicks Zed in File › Open Records In.
then: Expects VS Code when no valid editor is saved or a custom editor has no command; a known editor opened by its bundle ID through `/usr/bin/open -b` on macOS and by its command elsewhere, and the default app for `system`; a custom command run through `/bin/sh` with the file as `$1`, never in its text; and the menu names VS Code, Default App and the custom command's first word. Expects VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Default App and Edit Settings File…, VS Code checked, and Zed chosen.

title: A row taking another record's ID is refused once
when: Loads a use case test whose ID is a specification's, which links name.
then: Expects one unique-id refusal naming data/specification.jsonl:1, and none of the links to the ID.

title: An ID another record has, of any kind, is refused
when: For each kind, loads a record with the ID of another kind's record, and a second row with the same ID in its own file.
then: Expects a record with another kind's ID refused.

title: refuses an ID that does not start with its parent's or domain's ID
when: Loads a UC requirement whose ID starts with another use case's ID than its parent's.
then: Expects an `id-prefix` refusal naming the parent and the prefix its ID must start with.

title: A link from a record of one product to a record of another is refused, whatever the relation; an ID in text is not a link
when: Points the flow step `EX-LEND-UC02-FL01-S01` of product EX to happen in `NX-V01`, a view of a second product.
then: Expects one `link-crosses-product` refusal on `happens_in` saying `EX-LEND-UC02-FL01-S01 is in product EX`.

title: An ID a record names in its text is kept as written, and makes no link
when: Loads records whose text names other records, one of them twice. Loads a use case whose goal names another record twice, and its own ID. Loads a domain whose description names a specification MX-D-SP99 that does not exist, then adds a command with a `checks` link to it. Loads two products, where a use case's text names a record of the other product. Loads a use case whose text names another record of the product by its ID. Loads a domain whose description names the product and the domain by their bare IDs, in plain text and in a code span. Loads a product whose description names a bare product or domain ID in a code span. Loads a use case whose goal names IDs in a code span and in a fenced code block. On a temporary product, sets a requirement's statement naming this product's and another product's IDs, one in a code span. Shows the record and runs lathe check. On a temporary product, sets a requirement's statement to text naming records of this product and another, one in a code span. Shows the requirement and calls check.
then: Expects the text kept as written, no links, and no list of named IDs on a record. Expects a record's text to keep an ID named twice, and its own ID. Expects the text accepted and the link refused as a foreign key. Expects the text kept, no link from the use case, and no problem about the other product's ID. Expects a use case's text naming another record kept as written, and no links. Expects a domain's description naming the product and the domain, in plain text and in a code span, kept exactly. Expects the product's description to keep its code span. Expects the use case's goal to keep the code span `` `EX-LEND-UC02` `` and the fenced block holding EX-LEND-UC94 exactly. Expects the text kept as written, no link added and nothing reported about the IDs. Expects the text shown as written with no links, and no problem about the IDs.

title: A token that is not an ID of this workspace is plain text and no problem
when: Loads a use case whose goal names `STD-CODE-R01` and `SYS-AUTH`, which are no IDs of the workspace. Loads a use case whose goal names an invariant ID no record has, and lists the engine's own checks. Loads text naming IDs that start with a domain's ID and a hyphen but that no record has. Loads text naming IDs with other prefixes, such as `STD-` and `SYS-`. Loads text naming IDs that records have and IDs that none has, then runs every check.
then: Expects text naming IDs that no record has, with unknown prefixes, to be kept and reported by nothing. Expects no problem for a missing rule named in text, and `data-refused` as the engine's only problem of its own. Expects text naming missing IDs with the domain's prefix kept, and no problem about them. Expects text naming STD- and SYS- IDs kept, and no problem about them. Expects no `unknown-id-in-prose` problem, and no problem naming an ID written in another record's text.

title: Every record ID a page shows is a real link to that record
when: Opens every page in the list and reads each record ID shown in code on the page and in the Checks panel.
then: Expects each such ID inside an `<a href>` whose path is that record's own page, with more than 50 IDs checked.

title: Folded rows open by button or arrow keys and stay open after visiting another page
when: On a domain page.
then: Expects use cases and aggregates folded with their counts, opens and closes a row by button and by the arrow keys (moving into it and back to its parent), uses Expand all, and expects open rows still open after visiting another page.
notes: Proved in app/test/tree.test.tsx by the cases: Folded rows open by button or arrow keys and stay open after visiting another page; A record page's wiki lists its children one level deep.

title: A folded use case or aggregate keeps its count of records
when: On a domain page.
then: Expects use cases and aggregates folded with their counts, opens and closes a row by button and by the arrow keys (moving into it and back to its parent), uses Expand all, and expects open rows still open after visiting another page.

title: A record ID named in text does not appear in the graph
when: Opens `DM-PAY-UC01`, whose goal names `DM-SHOP-UC01` and `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, then Shopping's domain page with a description naming `DM-SHOP-UC01`.
then: Expects two links, `DM-SHOP-UC01` and `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, each titled with its record's title; no `DM-SHOP-UC01` link in the facts' Links out and no `DM-SHOP-UC01` node in the graph neighborhood; and the domain's description linking `DM-SHOP-UC01`.

title: IDs in code blocks, code with other text, links and longer IDs are not linked; a lone-ID code span is
when: Renders Markdown naming a record ID in a code span with other text, a code block, a link, a longer ID and a lone-ID code span, and links mentions in HTML with nothing to link.
then: Expects no links for IDs in code blocks, code spans with other text, links or longer IDs, a link around a code span holding one lone ID, and HTML left unchanged when there is nothing to link.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link: every record row on the domain and record pages has exactly one row link, stretched over the row
when: Opens Shopping's domain page and the record pages of `DM-SHOP-UC01` and `DM-SHOP-CMD01`.
then: Expects every row of every `record-list` (each tree item's own row, and each plain row) that holds a record link to have exactly one `row-link`, whose href is a record's page.

title: No page shows a relation code as a heading or label
when: Opens every record of a workspace with a record of each kind.
then: Expects no heading, field label, table header, legend, label or caption to read as a relation code ("satisfies", "proves", "depends on", "proves this"), and the graph's edge and key labels and the ERD stage's line titles to read the meta-model's labels.

title: The record page shows the ID, kind, title, text fields as Markdown, parent and children
when: Opens a use case.
then: Checks in the wiki card its ID, its kind badge in its stage's color, its goal rendered as Markdown and its child requirements, and its data file and parent link; then checks that Markdown in a text field is rendered.

title: The record page shows links out and in, grouped and named by their labels, each clickable
when: Opens UC requirement `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, then follows its Traceability link to the flow step `DM-SHOP-UC01-FL01-S01`.
then: Expects the requirement's Designed by (`DM-SHOP-CMD01`, `DM-SHOP-UC01-FL01`, `DM-SHOP-UC01-FL01-S01`, `DM-V01`), Built by (`DM-SHOP-CMD01-H`) and Proved by (`DM-SHOP-UC01-R01-T01`), its facts' kind and Links in links; then the step's page with Fulfills `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, Invokes `DM-SHOP-CMD01` and Happens in `DM-V01`, each a link in its facts.

title: A record's text is sanitized before it is shown
when: Renders a text field holding a script, an image with an onerror handler and a javascript: link, and Markdown holding an iframe and an onclick.
then: Checks that none of them reaches the page or runs.

title: The record page lists every problem about the record
when: Opens a test whose file is missing, then a use case with no problems.
then: Checks that a test with a missing file shows its error and badge, and that a record with no problems says so.

title: A click on a row opens its record, and a click on its chevron or second link does what that control does
when: On Shopping's domain page, clicks a capability row's chevron, presses Left on its link, Cmd- and Ctrl-clicks the row and clicks its padding; then, with a followed pattern, clicks the pattern row's "followed by" use case link and its plain text.
then: Expects a click on `DM-SHOP-CAP01`'s chevron to unfold it and stay on the page, Left on its row link to fold it, Cmd- and Ctrl-clicks left to the browser with no navigation, and a plain click on the row's padding to open `/DM-SHOP-CAP01`; on a pattern row, a click on its followed by link `DM-SHOP-UC01` to open that use case, and a click on its plain text to open `/DM-PAT-AUDIT`.

title: Every record ID named in the text becomes a link to its record, with its title on hover
when: Renders Markdown naming `TL-LEND-DR01` twice and `TL-LEND-UC01` in a list, with their titles known.
then: Expects three `a.mention` links, each to its record's page with its title on hover (One loan at a time, Lend a tool), and the text otherwise unchanged.
notes: Proved in app/test/mentions.test.tsx by the cases: Every record ID named in the text becomes a link to its record, with its title on hover; A code span holding one lone record ID becomes a link, keeping its code style; A text field links the records of the space it names, never the record itself; On a record page the records a text field names are links that move within the app; A domain overview links the records its text names, and an ID inside a longer one only as the longer.

title: An ID-shaped token that names no record stays plain text
when: Finds the links in a use case's goal followed by its own ID, where the goal names a pattern, an invariant and an ID that is no record.
then: Expects a text field's links to be the records of the space it names, without the record's own ID, and an ID that is no record left as plain text.
notes: Proved in app/test/mentions.test.tsx by the cases: An ID-shaped token that names no record stays plain text; On a record page an unknown ID stays plain text.

title: Lists on group pages stay at ten rows
when: Gives aggregate `P-D-A3` 13 invariants and opens its Invariants group page.
then: Expects the Invariants (13) page to show a search box named "Filter invariants of P-D-A3/invariant".

title: A domain page opens one level deep, and Expand all opens the rest
when: On a domain page.
then: Expects use cases and aggregates folded with their counts, opens and closes a row by button and by the arrow keys (moving into it and back to its parent), uses Expand all, and expects open rows still open after visiting another page.
notes: Proved in app/test/tree.test.tsx by the cases: A domain page opens one level deep, and Expand all opens the rest; A product page lists its domains but none of their records.

title: A list of up to 10 items is plain; a longer one scrolls inside, with search, a count and a no-match message
when: Renders the long list with 10 and with 12 items.
then: Expects no search box at 10; at 12, a focusable scrolling region, a search box reached by Tab that filters by ID and by title, a count that follows it, a message when nothing matches, and Escape clearing the search.
notes: Proved in app/test/long-list.test.tsx by the cases: A list of up to 10 items is plain; a longer one scrolls inside, with search, a count and a no-match message; Every list in the spec pages stays at 10 rows and can be searched.

title: The wiki card's kind, each problem code and each column label link to their format pages
when: Opens a record page, a domain page, the Checks panel and a group page.
then: Expects the Kind row and a column label to link to the kind's page and its column, each problem code to its check's page, and a group's kind to its page.

title: A record action opens the record's own data file, which the shell finds from its ID
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: In the desktop app, on a record, clicks Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID in its facts, then right-clicks a record row, a graph node and the page title.
then: Finder shows the record's data file selected, the editor opens it at the record's line and the clipboard holds the record's ID; each right-click's native menu offers the same three, and each works.
